newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold looking for upside, seen a good buy.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold looking for upside, seen a good buy.

text.p: Gold continued to offer buying opportunities as current price levels had good support and technical indications were looking positive, Hong Kong dealers said on Thursday.
"We are heading in an upward trend but we can't expect too much," a dealing source in the colony said.
"There's a lack of players and prices are not too active. On the technical side, the price is encouraging and I see it moving higher in a steady slope," he said.
Gold opened slightly firmer on Thursday in line with silver prices on early buying, extending gains made in New York overnight.
Bullion closed at $381.40/70 an ounce in Hong Kong, after opening at US$381.20/70 against New York's $381.05/55 close on Wednesday and Hong Kong's previous close of $380.80/381.30.
"Silver's rebound to 496/498 U.S. cents supported the gold prices," a bullion dealer said.
A gold marketer said he was recommending his customers buy gold as the upside had not yet been breached.
"There will be no selling yet," he said, citing some minor physical movement and short covering.
"Once we reach $384 or $385 we might see some activity. We need a little bit more movement. I am recommending to buy, and there's still a couple more days left of that," he said.
Other dealers concurred, saying strong fourth quarter demand would give the market its fundamental strength.
"Gold's tone remains steady to firm. The downside has good support at $375, and upside resistance is seen at $385 to $392," Anderson Cheung at Swiss Bank Corporation said.
"I think gold will keep a range of US$375 to $392 in (the fourth quarter of 1996)," he said.
Local gold closed HK$6 up on Wednesday at $3,516. The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Society was -3.
